articles.title: Trump’s Golden Fleet Could Leave Taxpayers With $275 Billion Bill
articles.summary: President Trump's proposal for a massive new fleet of battleships is projected to cost American taxpayers an estimated $275 billion. The substantial cost highlights ongoing debates regarding defence spending priorities and the strategic expansion of naval power, amidst current operational hurdles.

articles.title: How the US Navy attempted to deliver 3,000 letters by missile
articles.summary: In 1959, the US Navy pioneered an unusual experiment, launching a guided missile from a submarine that carried 3,000 letters. The missile successfully traversed the distance to Florida in a mere 22 minutes. This demonstrated early capabilities of submarine-launched guided missile technology for rapid, long-range transport, highlighting strategic potential beyond its initial, unconventional postal delivery objective.

articles.title: Evolutionists Are Wrong: Here’s The Truth About the Mediterranean Salt Deposits
articles.summary: During the 1971 Deep Sea Drilling Project (DSDP), scientists discovered extensive evaporite deposits—salt layers—deep within the Mediterranean Sea floor's sediment layers. This significant geological finding provided crucial insights into ancient marine environments, past climatic shifts, and the Earth's hydrological history, invaluable for understanding planetary evolution.

articles.title: Experts and policymakers to meet at ‘World Landslide Forum’
articles.summary: India is set to host the 7th World Landslide Forum (WLF7) for the first time, scheduled from November 22-27 at Amrita Vishwa Vidyapeetham, Delhi NCR. This six-day international event will gather global experts to discuss and address critical issues related to landslides. Hosting WLF7 highlights India's commitment to scientific collaboration and disaster risk reduction, showcasing its active role in tackling global environmental challenges.

articles.title: Philippines nears deal to buy more BrahMos missiles – report
articles.summary: The Philippines is nearing a deal worth up to $800 million to acquire more BrahMos supersonic cruise missiles from India. This acquisition aims to significantly strengthen Manila's coastal defense capabilities, building upon their previous purchase. The move underscores the Philippines' strategic focus on bolstering its maritime security posture with advanced weaponry.

articles.title: Quad Navies launch Malabar 2026 multi-domain drills to strengthen Free and Open Indo-Pacific
articles.summary: Naval forces from the Quad nations – India, United States, Japan, and Australia – have commenced Exercise Malabar 2026. This advanced multi-domain training aims to significantly enhance operational coordination, interoperability, and collective maritime security in the Indo-Pacific. The exercise underscores strengthening strategic partnerships and readiness to address regional challenges, crucial for aspiring defence personnel.
